full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique CJ. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the order dated 16.03.2022 passed by the High Court Division Civil Revision No.822 of 2022 staying further proceeding of the Miscellaneous Execution Case No.02 of 2010 pending in the Court of District Judge, Chattagram. 

 2. On 22.09.2004, the respondent No.1 Md. Nurul Abser and others instituted Other Suit No.193 of 2004 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Chattogram impleading the respondent. Nos.1-4 as defendant Nos.1-4 and 3 others seeking a declaration that the Arbitration Agreement dated 15.03.2002 executed between the plaintiffs and the defendant No.1 and award dated 15.03.2002 given by Alhaj Dostagir Chowdhury were arbitrary, illegal and void and further declaration that the said award does not take way tenancy right of the plaintiffs in the suit premises as described in the schedule to the plaint and for further declaration that the defendants do not have any authority to evict the plaintiffs from the scheduled premises by virtue of the said award through Other Execution Case No.04 of 2004. The notices were served upon the defendant Nos.1-4, whereupon they entered appearance and filed an application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 151 of the Code on.27.10.2004 stating, inter alia, that admittedly the plaintiffs were inducted into possession of the suit premises as a temporary monthly tenants under the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-4 and 5-7 late Alhaj Abul Khair and, accordingly, a tenancy agreement was executed on 17.04.1995 between the plaintiffs and the, defendant Nos.1-4 and the predecessors of the defendant Nos.5- 7, It was also contended in the said application for rejection of the plaint that on 15.03.2002 an arbitration agreement was entered into between the plaintiffs and the contesting defendants. In the said arbitration agreement there was a stipulation that Alhaj Dostagir Hossain Chowdhury would be appointed as an Arbitrator with a view to resolve the dispute between the parties expeditiously. Said Arbitrator gave award on 15.03.2002. Copy whereof was duly served upon both the parties. On the basis of the said award, the plaintiffs did not take any step as contemplated under section 42 the Arbitration Act, 2001 within 60 days. The defendant No.1 invoked section 44 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 initiating other Execution Case No.4 of 2004 under Order XXI Rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure for recovery of possession of the suit premises. The execution case was initiated in the Second court of Assistant Judge, Chattagram. The judgment debtor entered in the said execution case and unsuccessfully filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Against which Civil Revision No.197 of 2004 was filed in the Court of District Judge, Chattagram which was dismissed. 

 5. The respondent No.1, thereafter, filed an application for stay of the further proceeding of the Miscellaneous Execution Case N0.02 of 2010 till disposal of Other Appeal No.51 of 2014 and Partition Suit No. 66 of 2022 which was also rejected by the order No.94 dated 08.03.2022 and order No.95 dated 09.03.2022. Against which, the respondent Md. Nurul Abser filed civil revisional application in the High Court Division and obtained Rule and ad-interim order of stay of further proceeding of Miscellaneous Execution Case No.02 of 2010 in Civil Revision No. 822 of 2022. Against which the present petitioners have filed this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal. 

 6. Mr. Ahsan-ul Karim, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the petitioners arc entitled to get execution of the award they obtained and the respondents interrupted the execution upon different pleas since 2004, the High Court Division most improperly stayed the further proceeding of the aforesaid Execution Case. 

 8. The principle applied by the High Court Division for staying the execution proceeding was not applicable in the facts of this case because this is not suit; rather petitioners had filed execution of the award given in an Arbitration Proceeding. An award is enforceable as a decree and it is final. Facts and circumstances of the instant case, it appears that the respondent No.1 took unprecedented steps so that the award could not be executed and the petitioners holder will never be able to realize the fruits of the award. 

 9. Considering the facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the High Court Division committed error of law in staying the further proceeding of the instant old Execution case. The petitioners are entitled to get, the award executed. 

 10. Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is disposed of. The Rule issued in Civil Revision No.822 of 2022 is hereby discharged. The Executing Court is directed to proceed with the Execution Case.
